title: The Transfiguration (6 August)
hookLine: the light on the mountain in high summer
carry: it is good to be here

cards: Some evenings in August the light does something strange. The sun drops low, the air goes gold, and an ordinary street, a parking lot, a friend's face across a table, suddenly looks lit from inside.

People try to photograph it. Then it's gone, and it's just dusk. In the first week of August the Church remembers a moment like that, on a mountain, when three fishermen saw their teacher's face shine like the sun.
And one of them, not knowing what to say, said something anyway.

teach.h: HIS FACE SHONE LIKE THE SUN.
teach.b: Matthew, Mark and Luke all tell it. Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain, apart. And there he's transfigured before them: his face shines like the sun, his clothes turn dazzling white.
Moses and Elijah appear, often read as the Law and the Prophets, talking with him. Luke adds what they talked about: his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Then Peter, who never could stay quiet, says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles." Three tents. Let's stay.

Mark adds, gently, that he didn't know what to say, because they were terrified. Then a bright cloud covers them, and a voice says: this is my beloved Son, hear ye him. When they look up, there's only Jesus.
And they go back down the mountain. That's the shape of it. A moment of glory, and nobody gets to build a house there.

teach.h: LORD, IT IS GOOD FOR US TO BE HERE.
teach.b: The Gospels set it just after Jesus first tells them he will suffer and die, and some readers have heard it as a gift for the hard road ahead: a glimpse to remember on Good Friday. The Gospels never name the mountain.

Tradition says Mount Tabor in Galilee, and a church stands there now. The feast is very old in the East, and in 1457 Pope Callixtus III extended it to the whole Western Church, on the sixth of August.
The Greek verb Matthew uses is the root of our word metamorphosis.

how: Catholics keep the feast of the Transfiguration on 6 August, hearing one of the Gospel accounts of Jesus shining on the mountain; the same Gospel is also read on the Second Sunday of Lent.

games.q: you're Peter on the mountain. Jesus is shining, Moses and Elijah are there, and you're terrified. what do you say?
o: let's make three tents and stay.
let's go back down and tell everyone.
games.why: he offers three tents. then a cloud covers them, and when they look up, only Jesus is there, and they go back down.

practice: Go to a window or outside if you can, near sunset or sunrise if possible, and pick one patch of sky or one wall the light falls on.
Watch the color shift, a cloud move, a brightness fade or grow, without photographing it or trying to keep it. If you pray, you can say Peter's line once: it is good to be here.

wordCard.voice: The Transfiguration. Jesus shining on the mountain before Peter, James and John, with Moses and Elijah beside him. Its feast is the sixth of August. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: he was transfigured, changed in form — the root of metamorphosis.
